Fix is small and mechanical: add npm test as a step (the root suite runs in ~34s). ⚠️ The repo's baseline is NOT green — re-measured 2026-08-03 (pm) at #218: 95 test files collected, 1099 tests, 30 failed / 1069 passed, 9 failing files. Six further files collect 0 tests and so count as failing *files* while contributing 0 failing tests. So this cannot be a hard gate until backlog 3c lands; land it as a non-blocking reporting step first, or gate on "no NEW failures vs. master". Found 2026-08-03 while verifying the 9-PR merge order.

bugs.title: NARROWED + DOWNGRADED 2026-08-03 — the reported mechanism is REFUTED; one real case survives.
bugs.notes: #205's atomic-delete pattern denies legitimate non-admin deletes of salesData/forecasts — the 2026-08-02 scan argued RTDB evaluates multi-path update() rules against the post-update tree, so the index rule's root.child('salesData').child($id).child('userId') lookup would already read null. root is the PRE-write snapshot (Firebase: the database "as it exists before the attempted operation"; newData is the only post-write view), so that lookup sees the record intact and all three paths of the atomic delete grant — salesData/$id on pre-write data.child('userId'), byUser/$owner/$id on $userId === auth.uid, byLocation on the pre-write root. .validate is skipped on delete. WHAT IS REAL: a legacy record carrying no userId field evaluates null !== auth.uid at database.rules.json:505 and is denied for its non-admin owner — where pre-#205 the collection-level ".write": "auth != null" cascade-granted it (git show 90a3560^:database.rules.json). Different mechanism, much smaller blast radius, and already bounded: the #205 session documented it in-code (sales-data-service.js:876-881) and gated it with scripts/audit-sales-forecast-ownership.js, which ran pre-deploy and found exactly one anomaly (a legacy forecasts/{uid}/{loc}/{ts} container, since exported and removed by the operator). Remaining action is a probe, not a fix: confirm no flat record lacks userId; if any exist, backfill userId — do NOT change the rules. ⚠️ An admin probe proves nothing: the global root admin .write at database.rules.json:3 cascades and cannot be revoked by a child .write:false (2026-07-25 lesson), so admin returns 200 regardless. The probe must be non-admin.

bugs.title: receipts root .write is "auth != null" with NO child rules at all — any authenticated account can PUT /receipts.json and REPLACE EVERY TENANT'S RECEIPTS in one request.
bugs.notes: database.rules.json:134. This is strictly worse than the salesData/forecasts cascade fixed on 2026-07-28, because there is not even a dead child rule underneath to fall back to — the root grant is the *only* rule governing the node. Whole-node destruction, not per-record tampering. Not folded into the sales/forecast PR deliberately: the rewards/receipts/queue census returns 28 client files, and with no child rules there is nothing to preserve legitimate writes once the root grant is removed — tightening it without routing every writer first would break all client receipt writes (the #125 atomic-update class). Needs: full writer census by node name (incl. inline <script> in HTML) → child ownership rules → then lock the root. Receipts records carry guestPhoneNumber/totalAmount, so a scoping field exists, unlike rewards. Found 2026-07-28 by the security review of the sales/forecast design.

bugs.title: userLocations/$uid is self-writable with no .validate — any user can assert membership of any location, and four other .write rules trust that assertion.
bugs.notes: database.rules.json:57 allows auth.uid === $uid with no constraint on which $locationId keys are written, and a live client path does exactly this (public/js/modules/access-control/services/subscription-service.js:540). bugs.title: Three live credentials are stored as PLAINTEXT env vars on all 119 deployed functions, while the project already has a defineSecret pattern for four others — and a prior audit pass scored this area "clean".
bugs.notes: firebase functions:list --json returns environmentVariables in the clear for every function: TWILIO_TOKEN, SENDGRID_API_KEY, GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY (the rest — TWILIO_SID/TWILIO_PHONE/GOOGLE_PLACE_ID/TWILIO_SIGNATURE_MODE/TWILIO_WEBHOOK_URL — are identifiers/config, not secrets). Meanwhile ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, MERAKI_SHARED_SECRET, INITIAL_ADMIN_SETUP_SECRET and PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY ARE correctly managed via defineSecret, so the fix is to extend an established in-repo pattern, not invent one. Three reasons this is worse than generic hygiene: (1) the values ride on all 119 functions rather than the handful that need them, so any function compromise or any principal holding cloudfunctions.functions.get reads all three; (2) TWILIO_TOKEN is security-load-bearing — it is the HMAC key behind the CRIT-07 webhook signature verification closed and live-enforced in June (#162/#164); if it leaks, that control fails open and the forge-a-guest-message vector (voucher redemption / queue ops / data deletion) reopens; (3) the 2026-07-04/05 audit pass recorded "hardcoded secrets (all via process.env/defineSecret())" as clean (see the checked-and-clean paragraph in the OWASP section) — that conflated *not hardcoded in source* with *properly managed*, the same over-trust-a-clean-scan shape as the retracted HIGH-08 CVE closure. Not public — reading them requires GCP project access, hence Medium not Critical. Fix: migrate the three to defineSecret + scope each to only the functions that consume it, then rotate all three (they were surfaced into a session transcript on 2026-07-26 during a routine deploy-time lookup, which is itself the point — they are trivially readable). Note functions/.env is gitignored and holds these locally (2026-06-16 LESSON) — rotation must update it or the next deploy re-publishes the old values. Found 2026-07-26 while checking a deploy timestamp.

bugs.title: SEVERITY CORRECTED 2026-07-26 (High → Low-Med) against 13 months of Twilio logs — the mechanism is real, the blast radius was overstated.
bugs.notes: Measured over 4,094 outbound WhatsApp messages (2025-06-27 → 2026-07-26): 4,027 delivered/read = 98.4%; only 67 failures total, of which 37 were 63016 (outside-window). booking_confirmation specifically: 60 sends, 56 delivered/read, 4 failed — and ZERO failures since 2025-12. The reason the freeform fallback mostly works is structural and was missed in the original analysis: this is a WhatsApp-inbound-first operation (4,173 inbound messages), so the guest has usually opened the 24-hour window before we reply. booking_status_update is the genuinely bad one — 22 of 39 undelivered — but concentrated in 2025-12 (12) and 2026-05 (6), and it has not fired since 2026-06-20. ⚠ Do NOT read the quiet recent months as a fix: outbound volume collapsed (274 May → 89 Jun → 60 Jul) and queue_table_ready has not fired since 2026-05-05, so the clean streak is *absence of exercise*, not health — the 2025-12 spike (14 failures in a high-volume month) is the honest predictor of what returns with volume. Still worth fixing structurally (approved templates are the only correct business-initiated path), just not as a fire. _Original trace (mechanism, still accurate):_ the flow is LIVE (booking-management.js:687 on create and :769 on status change, plus 2 admin-tool call sites, all POSTing sendGuestBookingNotification; a booking was created 2026-07-26 08:48) → sendBookingConfirmationTemplate → sendWhatsAppTemplate('booking_confirmation', …) → RTDB whatsapp-template-config/booking_confirmation is enabled=false with an EMPTY contentSid → the freeform fallback path. A freeform message is deliverable only inside the customer-service window the guest opens by messaging us; a booking confirmation is business-initiated, so for any guest who hasn't messaged recently Twilio accepts it, returns a sid, and Meta never delivers it. 6 of 8 templates are in this state (booking_confirmation, booking_reminder, booking_status_update, queue_manual_addition, receipt_confirmation, welcome_message); only admin_new_booking_notification and ross_daily_digest have ContentSids. receipt_confirmation is fine in practice — it replies inside a guest-initiated conversation. booking_reminder has NO caller at all (dead code — reminders aren't silently failing, they're simply never sent). Partially addressed by this PR (degradation now logs at ERROR + statusCallback wiring + staged enforce refusal), but the actual remediation is external: get the business-initiated templates approved by Meta and set their ContentSids. Operator: quantify the damage in the Twilio console ✅ DONE 2026-07-26 — that measurement is what produced the correction above.

bugs.title: rossCreateRun dedupes on "any OPEN run", not "a run for this period" — so a run left open in a past cycle is returned forever and the next cycle's responses land in the wrong record.
bugs.notes: functions/ross.js:1523 queries orderByChild('completedAt').equalTo(null).limitToFirst(1) and returns that run with created: false. The founder's weekly workflow has had a run open since 2026-06-17; once the recurrence advance rolls it into a new cycle, opening the workflow returns that June run with its June responses pre-filled, and _countCompletedRequiredTasks counts them toward the new cycle. Pre-existing — the recurrence-advance job neither creates nor worsens it (and deliberately does NOT write to run records: papering over this by force-closing runs would put compliance history at risk). Fix options: dedupe on the run's period (store the cycle's nextDueDate on the run and match it) rather than on openness; or expire/abandon a run whose period has passed, with an explicit abandonedAt rather than a completedAt that would masquerade as completion in the digest. Needs a small schema decision. Found 2026-07-26 by the recurrence-advance design review.

bugs.title: LIVE TODAY — the admin new-booking notification fails more often than it succeeds, and every real template send fails 100%. Error 21211 (invalid 'To' number), not the 24-hour window.

Consequence: you are not reliably being told a booking arrived, and the one code path that uses an approved template has never worked. This is a config/data bug, not a Meta-approval problem — it does not wait on the template submission and is much cheaper to fix. Start by checking the admin recipient number(s) actually stored/configured for that notification (21211 = Twilio rejected the destination as malformed — confirm the exact semantics in Twilio's error reference), then the 21656/63032 cases, which look content/template-configuration shaped rather than window-shaped. Ranked above the template work, which the same measurement de-escalated.

bugs.title: Every RTDB rule written against auth.token.phone_number GRANTS instead of denying — no user in this app has that claim.
bugs.notes: There is no phone-based sign-in anywhere in the client (rg "signInWithPhoneNumber|RecaptchaVerifier|PhoneAuthProvider" public → zero hits; the only paths are createUserWithEmailAndPassword/signInWithEmailAndPassword), and every setCustomUserClaims call writes only {admin} and overwrites the whole claims object (functions/index.js:782,987,992,1321). So auth.token.phone_number is null for everyone — and RTDB evaluates null === null as TRUE, so any rule comparing it against a data.child(...) value that is also null (i.e. on a CREATE) grants rather than denies. This is not theoretical: it silently defeated the first draft of PR #176's rewards fix, caught by security review before deploy. Still to re-derive under this light: guest-rewards/$phoneNumber (database.rules.json:88) — its .write is admin || auth.token.phone_number === $phoneNumber, which is never true for a real user, so that node is effectively admin-only in practice (and is one reason receipt-management's reward flow is broken end-to-end, see the row below). Audit every remaining phone_number rule and replace null-mismatch reliance with explicit existence tests. Found 2026-07-21 via the PR #176 security review.

bugs.title: receipt-management.js reward creation is rejected by rules and has been for a long time — the flow is broken END TO END.
bugs.notes: processRewards (public/js/receipt-management.js:952-964) writes a reward payload of {receiptId, campaignId, guestPhoneNumber, totalAmount, status, createdAt, createdBy}, but rewards/$rewardId .validate requires newData.hasChildren(['metadata','status','value','expiresAt']) — the payload has status only, and the hasChildren term is an unconditional AND that not even an admin bypasses. The two follow-on writes fail as well: campaign-rewards/{cid}/{rid} requires admin (database.rules.json:93,96) and guest-rewards/{phone}/{rid} requires auth.token.phone_number === $phoneNumber (:88), which per the row above is null for every user. Sibling reward-management.js:661 (manual reward issue) supplies all four keys and works — presumably why this went unnoticed. Fix: add the missing fields to the payload (mirror reward-management.js:661), or route reward creation through a CF. Not bundled into PR #176 — it is a client payload bug, not a rules bug. Third live bug a rules census has surfaced (after locations/ownerId and this), all three hidden behind a client catch that only console.errors. Found 2026-07-21 during the PR-1b census, independently confirmed by security review.

bugs.title: rewardsProcessor.js:646 modulo bias in generateFallbackCode
bugs.notes: crypto.randomBytes(6) then byte % 36 over-represents chars 0–3 by ~14% (256 % 36 = 4). Vastly better than the old Math.random(), but not uniform for a security-relevant voucher fallback code. Fix: rejection sampling (while (code.length < 6) { const b = randomBytes(1)[0]; if (b < 252) code += chars[b % 36]; }). ~0.09 extra bytes/code. Surfaced by the #111 auto-review (🟡, on already-merged OWASP-era code).

bugs.title: Recurrence-engine gap: nextDueDate never advances when daily workflow goes uncompleted
bugs.notes: Operator noted on PR #72 preview: "I see one workflow that hasn't been completed daily since it was created." rossSubmitResponse auto-completes the run when all required tasks are done, but does NOT advance the workflow's nextDueDate for the next cycle. A daily workflow created 10 days ago with no run completed reads as daysLate: 10 instead of rolling forward. Fix needs: (a) on run completion, advance nextDueDate by recurrence period (daily/weekly/...); (b) decide policy when a cycle is fully missed (e.g. nextDueDate advances on the next "create run" attempt OR via a scheduled CF that walks every workflow nightly). bugs.title: MEASURED 2026-07-28 — the retention debt now has numbers, and they change the priority: scanningData holds 101,197 records, wifiLogins 18,198, activeUsers 16,805.
bugs.notes: Counted by a shallow key sweep of all 57 top-level RTDB nodes (run while ground-truthing a separate finding). For scale: each scanningData record is a Meraki webhook payload containing a data.observations[] ARRAY, so 101k records is *millions* of individual device observations. Two consequences the un-measured row understated: (1) a shallow read of scanningData alone is large enough to time out a 10-minute CLI sweep, so this is a live query-cost and latency problem, not tidiness; (2) the observations carry clientMac device identifiers with timestamps, AP and signal strength — personal data under POPIA, retained indefinitely with no consumer anywhere in the codebase (grepped .js/.html/.vue: the only references are rules-probe canaries and the clear path itself). Retaining PII with no processing purpose is the liability; clearing it *reduces* exposure. Other counts for reference: guests 2,289 · whatsapp-message-history 2,086 · consent-history 590 · receipts 210 · guest-receipts 181 · receiptPatternLogs 144. Operator cleared scanningData manually on 2026-07-28 via firebase database:remove — that buys time and fixes nothing; the Meraki webhook (functions/index.js:475) refills it continuously. Scheduled pruning is queue card Q13. _Original row:_ same root cause: in-app "Clear X" buttons are time-bombs without scheduled pruning. Now covers /scanningData (PR #70), /wifiLogins, /activeUsers, /userPreferences, /rateLimitsWifi (all per PR #73), and /billing/debitGuard/{uid}/{requestId} (PR #134 review T-2 — the slice-3 requestId is a fresh UUID per request, so guard nodes never dedupe and accumulate ~1/turn forever; a TTL/expiresAt sweep or 90-day prune closes it), and /ross/agentPending/{uid}/{turnId} (PR #136 review M-3 — abandoned/expired confirm actions are never consumed, so they orphan; a scheduled prune of expiresAt < now − grace closes it — bundle into the slice 7 ross/agent* rules work), and /ross/proactiveLog/{uid}/{YYYY-MM-DD} (PR #158 review — daily nudge dedup markers, ~365 nodes/user/year; rossAgentPrune is the natural home for a 90-day sweep; add before opt-in widens past the founder). Options: (a) scheduled prune CF (onSchedule('every 24 hours')) using the chunked-delete pattern from clearScanningData, prune records older than 30/90 days; (b) TTL-on-write with expiresAt; (c) aggregate-then-discard to hourly/daily rollups. Needs product conversation on retention window per node (different windows likely OK — guest analytics may want 90d, rate-limits only need 1h).

bugs.title: Double-seed race on signup retry
bugs.notes: rossSeedFirstWorkflow's idempotency pre-check is not transactional. A user double-clicking signup or hitting a network retry could pass the pre-check in both invocations and produce two seeded workflows. Mitigation options: (a) RTDB transaction() on the firstWorkflowSeededAt marker, OR (b) deterministic workflow ID per uid (e.g. seed_{uid} rather than push key) so duplicate write is overwrite. Exposure small; consequence mild (duplicate workflow, no corruption).

bugs.title: Workflow task edit not reflected in restarted run
bugs.notes: operator changed a task's inputType (temperature → photo) via the Phase 4e.1 task editor, hit save, then started a new run on the workflow. The run UI still showed the old inputType. Could be (a) the task editor not actually persisting inputType despite the allowedFields list including it; (b) rossManageTask server-side update not landing; (c) getPlaybookWorkflows caching or stale-read; (d) the operator hit the server's "Run is already completed" 409 case and was viewing the OLD completed run's task snapshot, not a fresh workflow read. Investigation needed before fix.

bugs.title: Task editor UX needs single-Save + success feedback + auto-exit
bugs.notes: operator feedback on the Phase 4e.1 task editor (RossPlaybookWorkflowTasksEditor.vue): currently has a Save button per task row, and saving doesn't exit edit mode or confirm to the user. Desired: one Save button at the bottom that commits all dirty tasks, a success message, then auto-exit back to the workflow card view. Pre-existing scope from PR #32; not a Run-UI bug.

bugs.title: Subscription resolves "enterprise" tier for the operator's test account
bugs.notes: feature-access-control log on PR #65 preview shows Resolved tier ID: enterprise (from: tierId). Tier system is supposed to be free / all-in only (PR #51). The operator's account has a legacy tierId: 'enterprise' value somewhere in subscriptions/{uid}. Unclear whether enterprise is treated as super-tier (all-in equivalent) downstream — likely silently falls through. Fix: audit operator's subscription record + decide whether to backfill to all-in or formalize enterprise as a third tier.

bugs.title: Server auto-completes runs after a single response if workflow has small required-task count
bugs.notes: surfaced indirectly via PR #65 preview. Auto-completion check (functions/ross.js:1311-1314) treats all tasks with required !== false as required. The seeded Daily Opening Checklist has 4 subtasks but none carry an explicit required field — so all 4 are required, and auto-completion only fires when all 4 are responded. NOT actually a bug in the server logic per se, but: the operator hit "Run is already completed" 409, which implies SOMETHING auto-completed the run prematurely. Could be a separate run from an earlier test, OR a workflow with only 1 effective task. Worth a focused repro session before judging.

bugs.title: database.rules.json fails STRICT JSON.parse
bugs.notes: the bookings block (~line 302) embeds literal newlines inside rule-expression strings; Firebase CLI's lenient parser accepts it (deployed as-is for months) but JSON.parse, jq, and most tooling reject the file. Bit the PR #158 verification step (plan's parse check failed on a clean edit). Fix: normalize the multi-line rule strings to single-line (pure formatting, no semantic change), then strict-parse becomes a usable pre-deploy guard — candidate for guard-backfill 3c (a tiny vitest that JSON.parses the rules file).

bugs.title: The bigger silent-drop surface is freeform-by-design, not template degradation — queueWhatsAppIntegration.js sends the most time-critical guest messages with no template at all.
bugs.notes: "🔔 Your Table is Ready!", position updates and wait reminders (functions/queueWhatsAppIntegration.js:667-686) go through sendWhatsAppMessage — pure freeform, business-initiated (an admin clicks Notify), no template anywhere in the path. They are subject to the identical 24-hour-window drop as the booking confirmations above, and a table-ready message that arrives never is worse than most failures in the product. The 2026-07-26 PR gives them statusCallback (so failures at least become observable) but deliberately does NOT classify or enforce them — enforcement without an approved template would simply block the send. Fix: a queue_table_ready content template through Meta approval, then route these via sendWhatsAppTemplate. Same external long-pole as the booking templates; worth batching into one Meta submission. Found by the security review of that PR. Measured 2026-07-26 (Twilio logs): 22 sends lifetime, 18 read / 1 delivered / 3 undelivered (63016) — a 13.6% drop rate, worse than booking confirmations. But it has not fired since 2026-05-05, so its clean recent record is un-exercised, not healthy; treat the 13.6% as the live rate whenever the queue is next used in anger.
